records.question: How much money is behind Genesis, and how much of it is real cash?
records.answer: Genesis carries more than $5 billion in announced federal commitments, more than $800 million in partner support and $2.4 billion in October company pledges, but none of it is shown as cash paid: only 1 line includes obligated money, 2 are selections for award and 2 are open calls.

records.question: Which companies are Genesis members, which only pledged, and which have named project roles?
records.answer: Of the 63 companies in the Genesis record, 46 are on the consortium's private-sector roster (checked October 13, 2026), 11 pledged support in October (5 of them without being on the roster), and 20 have a named role on a specific project.

records.question: Who received the 278 Genesis project selections, and where are they?
records.answer: All 278 July 22 selections are 'selected for award negotiations' with no dollar amounts published; they sit in 45 states, led by CA (56), NY (25), WA (18), and the busiest lead is Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) with 16.

records.question: What are the 33 science challenges the Genesis Mission is meant to solve?
records.answer: DOE's July 22, 2026 document lists 33 science and technology challenges in five areas: Protecting the Nation from Emerging Threats (9), Extending the Frontiers of American Discovery (8), Delivering Reliable Infrastructure and Energy Affordability (7), Building American Industrial Strength (5), Helping Americans Live Longer, Healthier Lives (4). They include 'Delivering Nuclear Energy That is Faster, Safer, Cheaper', 'Scaling the Grid to Power the American Economy', 'Software Understanding for National Security', 'Ensuring American Space Superiority'. All 33 are proposed objectives in DOE's text, not measured results; only 2 have a profiled Genesis project assigned: GridFM 2.0 (to 'Scaling the Grid to Power the American Economy') and Prometheus nuclear AI (to 'Delivering Nuclear Energy That is Faster, Safer, Cheaper').

records.question: Which exact legal company holds each NSSTS role, and who owns it?
records.answer: The NSSTS registries name 16 legal entities that recur across sectors: 9 are subsidiaries held by a larger company (for example Amazon Web Services, Inc., owned by Amazon.com, Inc.), 3 are top companies, and for 4 the registries record no owner; 1 acquired company is still listed on its own and is shown here under its owner.

records.question: Which shared bottlenecks do several NSSTS programs depend on, and which are overdue for a check?
records.answer: 15 shared bottlenecks sit under the NSSTS programs; the widest, OTA and consortium prototype-to-production transition, touches 6 sectors and 19 company positions, and 6 of the 15 are past their check date with no newer check on record.

records.question: If one NSSTS program fails, what else breaks, and what are the warning signs?
records.answer: The package traces 18 failure chains; the widest (“A transformer factory delay, failed FITT field test, or unaccepted transformer delivery constrains a major project interconnection”) reaches 5 sectors. 15 of the 18 are rated high immediacy, and 2 are past their re-check date with no newer check.

records.question: Which dated decisions in the next year will show whether each NSSTS company's position is real?
records.answer: 34 dated decisions across 12 companies run from August 27, 2026 to December 31, 2027; 2 have passed with no recorded outcome, and the next is due October 31, 2026 (BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration Inc.).

records.question: Which lesser-known contractors, testers and insurers sit underneath the big national-security tech programs?
records.answer: The science plan's structural map names 48 firm entries (45 different names; a few firms sit in more than one corridor), and 19 kinds of firm, beneath the headline programs in 8 corridors. In AI compute: WWT, SambaNova and the engineers Bridgers & Paxton, Burns & McDonnell and Sargent & Lundy. On the grid: study and test firms such as Qualus, PowerGEM, Doble and Shermco. In quantum and encryption: Bluefors, FormFactor, Entrust and SafeLogic. In minerals and nuclear: SRK, NAC International and the insurer-engineer FM Approvals. 46 of the 48 entries match a row in an NSSTS registry (by name, or by row id where no name matched). The map says these firms do not inherit final authority, and it cites no source per corridor.

records.question: Where are the national-security tech programs physically built, and which sites are still secret or undecided?
records.answer: The program registry places 13 sites. 3 are verified program sites (Eaton FITT project location, Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin; GE Vernova FITT project location, Schenectady, New York; Lockheed Martin GPS IIIF production facility, Denver / Littleton, Colorado). 3 are verified company sites where the program's own work is not shown (Argonne Leadership Computing Facility / Building 240, Lemont, Illinois; nLIGHT beam-combined HEL manufacturing expansion, Longmont, Colorado; Lockheed Martin Aculight high-energy-laser operations, Bothell, Washington). 2 are planned or being built (Natcast Advanced Packaging Piloting Facility, ASU Research Park, Tempe, Arizona (planned); Amkor advanced packaging and test facility, Peoria, Arizona). 5 are not publicly disclosed or not yet decided: NNSA Secret/Restricted Data Enterprise Cloud physical hosting environment; Distributed Bioindustrial Production Capability prototype site; QTIME performer and transition-user test locations; Space Data Network satellite, gateway and integration sites; Protected Tactical SATCOM spacecraft integration and checkout sites.
